'''Mònica Dòria Vilarrubla''' (born 4 December 1999) is an Andorran [[Canoe slalom|slalom canoeist]] who has competed at the international level since 2014.<ref>{{cite web |title=Monica DORIA VILARRUBLA (AND) |url=https://canoeslalom.net/doku.php/en_sportler/spo_14190d |website=CanoeSlalom.net |accessdate=13 February 2021}}</ref> Mònica was the flagbearer for [[Andorra at the 2020 Summer Olympics]] and at the [[Andorra at the 2024 Summer Olympics|2024 Summer Olympics]].<ref>{{cite news|title=La palista Mònica Dòria será la abanderada de Andorra en Tokio 2021|trans-title=Canoeist Mònica Dòria will be Andorra's flag bearer in Tokyo 2020|publisher=[[Europa Press (news agency)|Europa Press]]|url=https://www.europapress.es/catalunya/andorra-01111/noticia-palista-monica-doria-sera-abanderada-andorra-tokio-2021-20210625153440.html|access-date=29 July 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.altaveu.com/actualitat/esport/doria-carabana-ja-es-preparen-cerimonia-inaugural-jocs-olimpics-paris_59134_102.html|trans-title=Doria and Carabaña are already preparing for the opening ceremony of the Olympic Games in Paris|language=Catalan|title=Doria i Carabaña ja es preparen per a la cerimònia inaugural dels Jocs Olímpics de París|last=Escola|first=Marco|date=23 July 2024|website=www.altaveu.com|publisher=Altaveu|access-date=25 July 2024}}</ref>

== Career ==
Dòria won two medals at the [[ICF Canoe Slalom World Championships]] with a silver in the C1 event in [[2026 ICF Canoe Slalom World Championships – Women's C1|2026]] and a bronze in kayak cross in [[2022 ICF Canoe Slalom World Championships – Women's extreme kayak|2022]].

She also won a gold medal in the C1 event at the [[2025 European Canoe Slalom Championships|2025 European Championships]] in [[Vaires-sur-Marne]].

At the 2020 Olympics, she finished 16th in the [[Canoeing at the 2020 Summer Olympics – Women's slalom K-1|K1 event]] and 11th in the [[Canoeing at the 2020 Summer Olympics – Women's slalom C-1|C1 event]] after being eliminated in the semifinals of both.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Results (Tokyo K1)|url=https://olympics.com/tokyo-2020/olympic-games/resOG2020-/pdf/OG2020-/CSL/OG2020-_CSL_C73A_CSLWK1----------------SFNL000100--.pdf|access-date=29 July 2020|website=Olympics|language=ja|archive-date=27 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210727132959/https://olympics.com/tokyo-2020/olympic-games/resOG2020-/pdf/OG2020-/CSL/OG2020-_CSL_C73A_CSLWK1----------------SFNL000100--.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Results (Tokyo C1)|url=https://olympics.com/tokyo-2020/olympic-games/resOG2020-/pdf/OG2020-/CSL/OG2020-_CSL_C73A_CSLWC1----------------SFNL000100--.pdf|access-date=29 July 2020|website=Olympics|language=ja|archive-date=29 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210729103435/https://olympics.com/tokyo-2020/olympic-games/resOG2020-/pdf/OG2020-/CSL/OG2020-_CSL_C73A_CSLWC1----------------SFNL000100--.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref>

At the [[2024 Paris Olympics]], Dòria competed in the [[Canoeing at the 2024 Summer Olympics – Women's slalom K-1|K1 event]], [[Canoeing at the 2024 Summer Olympics – Women's slalom kayak cross|kayak cross]] and the [[Canoeing at the 2024 Summer Olympics – Women's slalom C-1|C1 event]], finishing in 22nd place, 15th place and 6th place respectively.<ref>{{cite web |title=Women's Kayak Single - Semifinal results |url=https://olympics.com/OG2024/pdf/OG2024/CSL/OG2024_CSL_C73C1_CSLWK1----------------SFNL000100--.pdf |website=[[Olympics.com]] |access-date=3 December 2024 |date=28 July 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://olympics.com/OG2024/pdf/OG2024/CSL/OG2024_CSL_C74X2_CSLWX1----------------------------.pdf|title=Canoe Slalom - Women's Kayak Cross - Individual Medals and Ranking|website=Olympics.com|date=4 August 2024|access-date=3 December 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Women's Canoe Single - Finals results |url=https://olympics.com/OG2024/pdf/OG2024/CSL/OG2024_CSL_C73C1_CSLWC1----------------FNL-000100--.pdf |website=Olympics.com |access-date=3 December 2024 |date=31 July 2024}}</ref>

She won a gold medal in the C1 event at the [[2017 European Junior and U23 Canoe Slalom Championships|2017 Junior European Championships]] in [[Hagen-Hohenlimburg|Hohenlimburg]], [[Germany]]. She earned her best senior world championship results of 8th and 30th (C1 and K1, respectively), at the [[2019 ICF Canoe Slalom World Championships]] in [[Segre Olympic Park|La Seu d'Urgell]].<ref name="thesports"/> These results secured her a quota place for the [[2020 Summer Olympics]] in Tokyo, where she represented Andorra in the [[Canoeing at the 2020 Summer Olympics|C1 and K1 events]]. This was only the second time Andorra has been represented in canoe slalom at the Olympic Games, after [[Montserrat García Riberaygua]] competed in the [[Canoeing at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Women's slalom K-1|K1 event]] at the [[2008 Summer Olympics|2008 Beijing Olympics]].<ref>{{cite web |title=MONTSERRAT GARCIA RIBERAYGUA |url=https://www.olympic.org/montserrat-garcia-riberaygua |website=Olympic.org |accessdate=13 February 2021}}</ref>

She is based in [[Spain]] but competes for [[Andorra]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Monica DORIA VILARRUBLA (AND)|url=https://www.canoeicf.com/athlete/monica-doria-vilarrubla|website=ICF - Planet Canoe|date=21 September 2019 |language=en|accessdate=13 February 2021}}</ref>
